title: Audit and fix canonical link tags across all zedu.chat marketing pages
description: Inspect all primary marketing pages (home, /pricing, /products/buzz, /products/channels, /products/file-management, /download, and /solutions/*) for rel=canonical link elements. Record the exact tag present on each page, identify pages missing canonical declarations or pointing to staging/relative URLs, and write paste-ready Next.js metadata canonical configurations for each page. Deliver the audit table and code in the attachment.

goal.title: Improve Zedu on-page content SEO
goal.description: Optimise Zedu’s page titles, meta descriptions, headings, keywords, alt text and internal links so each page ranks better and drives more organic traffic.

workstream.title: One pass to fix every on-page defect, then publish the content the site is already promising
workstream.description:
Two linked pieces of work, both driven by measurement of the live site rather than by guesswork.

The first is a fix pass over the sixteen public marketing pages, delivered as a page-by-page table of every title, description, H1 and canonical with the current value, the problem and the replacement side by side. The measurement behind it: the homepage title tag is 'Home'; every marketing page's meta description runs past 160 characters, from 168 to 185, so search engines truncate them all; the homepage ships nine H1 elements against twenty-two H2s, and /about has five, /pricing four, the solution pages six or seven and the product pages three or six; /policy, /terms-of-service and /resources share one generic title with no canonical tag; /auth/login and /auth/sign-up are indexable with the title 'Zedu' and no description; and /blog and /products return HTTP 200 but render a login screen to a visitor.

The second is the content the site already promises and does not have. The /resources page lists four guide cards, every one of them links to '#', and the same four cards repeat three times in the served content. Four publish-ready articles turn four live dead links into real destinations: managing a bootcamp cohort, coordinating one university course across lectures, labs and projects, keeping one K-12 class organised and catching the pupil who goes quiet, and what an AI assistant should and should not handle. Each article is one concrete scenario written for one audience, with a title under 60 characters, a description under 160 characters, a three-question FAQ, and the internal links to add, each with exact anchor text.

Every current value and every proposed value is copied from the live markup so it can be checked directly, and no URL is recommended for removal without the overlap being demonstrated. Robots.txt and sitemap.xml are deliberately out of scope because another workstream in this project covers them.
